title: Singapore's review of Australia's under-16 social media ban and age assurance plans
asked: Mr Vikram Nair asked whether the Ministry of Digital Development and Information has completed its review of Australia's legislation banning social media access for under-16s, and if so, whether Singapore will consider similar legislation.
response: The Minister of State said Australia's social media minimum age regulations took effect on 10 December 2025, and MDDI is engaging Australian counterparts and assessing their effectiveness. Singapore has imposed age assurance requirements on designated app stores, expected by 31 March 2026, and plans to extend them to designated social media services. Consultations with social media services are ongoing, and she said there is no silver bullet because children can circumvent measures, so MDDI will work with people, private and public sectors on resources for parents.

key_points.point: Australia's social media minimum age regulations came into effect on 10 December 2025.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: Australia's social media minimum age regulations came into effect on 10 December 2025.

key_points.point: MDDI is actively engaging Australian counterparts and assessing the effectiveness of the measures in Australia.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: The Ministry of Digital Development and Information (MDDI) is actively engaging our Australian counterparts and assessing the effectiveness of the measures in Australia.

key_points.point: Designated app stores are expected to implement age assurance measures by 31 March 2026.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: Designated app stores are expected to implement these age assurance measures by 31 March 2026.

key_points.point: MDDI plans to extend age assurance requirements to designated social media services.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: We also plan to extend age assurance requirements to designated social media services to reduce children's exposure to age-inappropriate content on social media platforms.

key_points.point: Consultations with designated social media services are ongoing.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: Consultations with designated social media services are ongoing.

key_points.point: The age assurance measures will come on top of existing protective measures under the current Code of Practice for Online Safety – Social Media Services.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: The age assurance measures will come on top of the existing protective measures for children under the current Code of Practice for Online Safety – Social Media Services.

key_points.point: A child can still circumvent these measures, such as through using an adult's account to access age-inappropriate content.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: A child can still circumvent these measures, such as through using an adult's account to access age-inappropriate content.

key_points.point: Australia's implementation challenges include migration of children or users to platforms not within the regulatory ambit.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: There was an observation that there was a migration of children or the users to platforms that are not within the regulatory ambit.

key_points.point: The ministry looks at three main things: screen time and addiction, inappropriate content, and undesirable online behaviours such as cyber bullying.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: There are three main things that we look at.

key_points.point: Age assurance methods are not prescribed; platforms may use age verification or age estimation.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: We have not been prescriptive with how age assurance measures are put in, because even for age assurance, you have age verification and age estimation.

key_points.point: MDDI will work with people, private and public sectors to co-create resources and programmes for parents.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: MDDI will continue to work with partners from the people, private and public sectors, to co-create resources and programmes that are convenient and accessible for parents to help guide their children to foster healthy digital habits from young.

left_open: Whether the Ministry has completed its review of Australia's move.
Whether Singapore will introduce similar legislation banning social media access for under-16s.
Whether social media platforms are required to prevent young users from using their platforms.
supplementary: Supplementary questions focused on whether platforms must block underage use and on addiction versus harmful content.
